$comment: Surface parity, not behaviour. Asserts every SDK EXPOSES the v1 control-point surface. Behavioural fixtures live in contracts/. Rationale: nothing structurally forces seven independent implementations to agree, and a missing method is invisible — go shipped client.Flags() with no ControlPoints namespace, and python shipped get_integer_value with no object variant, both unnoticed for months. A parity fixture turns that from a silent divergence into a failing cell.

methods.name: getNumberValue
methods.$comment: number, NOT integer. python currently exposes get_integer_value — that is the drift this row catches.

methods.name: getObjectValue
methods.$comment: REQUIRED. python has no object variant today.

methods.name: getObjectDetails
methods.$comment: All four *Details are absent from every SDK today.

methods.name: registerTarget
methods.$comment: Local mode records the target in-process and emits one trace line naming the mode; it returns ok:true. Silent success — recording without the trace — is a conformance failure, because the trace is what stops a dev harness looking registered without saying so.

client.$comment: mustNotExpose is the v1 scope boundary AND the OpenFeature removal, asserted rather than trusted.
